entities.name: Secondary amenorrhea
observations: Usually defined as absent menses for at least 3 months in a woman with previously regular cycles.
Initial evaluation of established cases excludes pregnancy, then commonly includes TSH and prolactin; FSH with estradiol helps distinguish ovarian from hypothalamic or pituitary causes.

entities.name: Post-pill 2-month amenorrhea
observations: In a previously regular, low-risk patient, 2 months without menses after stopping oral contraception does not yet meet the usual definition of secondary amenorrhea; short-term observation until 3 months is reasonable.
Serum beta-hCG is reasonable if immediate formal evaluation is desired despite negative urine tests, but progesterone challenge, ultrasound, and FSH/estradiol are not mandatory immediately.
